response.text:
Quick clarification — do you mean:
- "Archive the messages that have the label 'contracts 2019' (i.e., archive those emails)?" or
- "Delete the label 'contracts 2019' (remove the label itself)?"  

I'll explain both below so you're covered.

If you archive the messages with that label
- The messages are removed from your Inbox view but are kept in your account (they go to "All Mail").  
- The messages remain searchable and accessible, and any labels that were on them remain (so you can still open them from the label).  
- This is reversible and not time-limited — archived mail is not automatically deleted.

If you delete the messages with that label (i.e., delete the emails)
- The messages are moved to Trash. They can be restored from Trash for up to ~30 days.  
- After the Trash retention period they are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.  
- This is a destructive action if you let it pass the Trash period.

If you delete the label itself (i.e., remove the label, not the emails)
- The label is removed from those messages, but the messages themselves remain in your account (All Mail or Inbox).  
- Deleting a label does not delete the messages — it only removes that label/tag. You can still find the messages by search or other labels.  
- If you recreate the label later, existing messages won’t automatically get that label back unless you relabel them.

Other practical notes
- Archiving keeps history and is safe if you just want to tidy your Inbox.  
- Deleting messages frees space (eventually) but is potentially irreversible after Trash is emptied or 30 days pass.  
- Deleting a label is useful if you only want to remove the classification without touching message content.  
- If you’re unsure, archive or remove the label rather than permanently deleting messages. You can also back up important threads first.

If you tell me which of the three actions you actually intended, I can give exact steps and a safe checklist so you don’t lose anything by accident.
